title: A Chameleon's Tongue Hits 60 mph in One Hundredth of a Second

scenes.text: A chameleon's tongue goes zero to sixty in a hundredth of a second.
That's 264 g. A fighter jet pulls about nine.
The tongue shoots out two and a half body lengths. The cricket is gone in 20 milliseconds.
It's loaded like a slingshot. Stretched collagen fires it, not muscle.
And the smaller the chameleon, the faster the shot. A thumb-sized one holds the record.
Zero to sixty. By the time you finish blinking, it's already over.

description:
A chameleon's tongue accelerates from zero to sixty miles an hour in about a hundredth of a second.
Brown University filmed 20 species with high-speed cameras: the tiny Rhampholeon spinosus hit 264 g, the highest acceleration ever measured in a reptile, bird or mammal, and reached a cricket in about 20 milliseconds.
Which animal would you least want to be in a reaction-time contest with?
first_comment: The tongue is powered by stretched collagen, like a slingshot, so even a cold chameleon can fire it at full speed. What is the fastest animal move you have seen in real life?
